page: Amazon Web Services g5.xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server powered by an AMD EPYC 7R32 processor running at 3.3 GHz. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores with hyperthreading, 16.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, and a 250 GB NVMe SSD for local storage. The instance is equipped with a single NVIDIA Ampere A10G GPU providing 22 GB of VRAM, and operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor with a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals a stark contrast between CPU-bound tasks and GPU-accelerated workloads. The server exhibits weak to poor performance in standard CPU and memory benchmarks, with stress-ng single-core and multi-core metrics falling into the bottom 10%, and memory bandwidth tests ranking in the bottom 25%. However, the integrated NVIDIA A10G GPU delivers top-tier performance for machine learning workloads. LLM inference speeds for both prompt processing and text generation using small (135M) and medium (7B) models consistently rank in the top 10% of tested servers.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the g5.xlarge offers a highly specialized resource profile. While it represents a high-density GPU entry point, the trade-off is limited CPU compute and memory bandwidth. Consequently, this server is poorly suited for CPU-heavy compilation, database operations, or high-throughput web serving. Instead, it is optimized for GPU-accelerated workloads such as small-to-medium LLM inference, graphics-intensive applications, and machine learning model evaluation where the GPU can be fully utilized while keeping CPU overhead minimal.
